voice.name: en-GB-SoniaNeural
voice.prosody: Once, 4,000 people lived inside these walls, and much of the world was ruled from here. After taking Istanbul, Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror built this palace on the city's finest point, Sarayburnu, with the sea on three sides. For about 380 years the Ottoman sultans lived here and ran the empire from here. The palace is not one building but a town of courtyards, one inside another. Anyone could enter the first courtyard. The further in you go, the narrower the gates and the stricter the rules. The innermost courts belonged only to the sultan and his circle. The Harem was the private, closed-off home of the sultan's family. Today you can see the sultans' treasures, their kaftans and the sacred relics. There is always a small crowd in front of the Spoonmaker's Diamond. Then walk out onto the terrace in the last courtyard: the Bosphorus, the Golden Horn and the Sea of Marmara lie in front of you at once. Don't miss the palace kitchens. Food was once cooked here for thousands of people, and today they hold one of the richest collections of Chinese porcelain in the world. The sultans' table was as famous as their treasury.
